data.title: FireFly Metals Highlights Green Bay Exploration Upside with Second Major Copper-Gold Discovery in a Month
data.description:
FireFly Metals has made a second significant copper-gold discovery in a month at its Green Bay project in the Baie Verte district of north-east Newfoundland in Canada.

Located less than 10 kilometres from the company’s mothballed Ming undergound mine, the Nash volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) discovery was initially identified by an airborne electromagnetic survey completed in 2024.

Follow-up mapping and surface prospecting in the area of a +3km conductive anomaly hosting Nash and the earlier RDI target identified widespread mineralisation in approximately 44 rock chip samples, returning grades as high as 19.8% copper.

Maiden drilling at Nash targeted areas of coincident geophysical and geochemical anomalism, with the results confirming the presence of shallow mineralisation through intersections of 26.7m at 2.3% copper from 9m including a high-grade zone of 9.6m at 4.6%.

The RDI target, located 1.1km from the Nash discovery along the same geophysical trend, returned a maiden shallow intersection of 11.2m at 1.2% copper from 15.9m including 4m at 2.3% after its discovery earlier this month.

Mount Joy System

Firefly identified the high-grade Mount Joy copper-gold system in October after drilling at the previously untested target returned 22.5m at 2.5% copper equivalent from 109m including 9m at 3.9% CuEq.

Mount Joy—which lies 35km east of the Ming mine and 2.6km from the Nugget Pond processing facility, which remains on care and maintenance—emerged from recent airborne electromagnetic surveys, ground-based follow-up work, and geochemical prospecting across the Tilt Cove-Betts Cove VMS district.

At the time, managing director Steve Parsons said the discovery underscored the “immense potential” of the geophysical and geochemical targets identified at Green Bay, supporting a plan to continue driving growth in the project’s mineral resource, mine life, and forecast production rates.

Green Bay Resource

Green Bay’s current mineral resource estimate sits at 60.2 million tonnes grading 2.4% CuEq in the higher confidence Measured and Indicated categories, plus a further 23.5Mt at 2.5% CuEq inferred.

An update is being targeted for early in the new year followed by a feasibility study relating to a 1.8Mt per annum production restart scenario at Ming, which has existing underground access including a decline to 950m and a 650m shaft used for drilling and development.

FireFly has been granted an exclusive option to acquire the contiguous Brass Buckle property less than 10km southeast of Ming.

Brass Buckle comprises 16.5 square kilometres of highly prospective exploration claims immediately adjacent to the Nash discovery.

data.title: U.S. Treasurys Edge Lower Amid Higher Fed Rate-Hike Prospects — Market Talk
data.description: U.S. Treasurys edge lower in price terms in the Asian session amid higher prospects for Fed rate hikes. Wall Street's surge on Monday "offered some relief to the tech sector thanks to Nvidia's funding of the AI ecosystem and following Friday's sharp market slide," NAB's Gavin Friend says in commentary. data.title: Macquarie Led Group to Buy Axiata's International Towers in $1.2 Billion Deal — Update
data.description:
By P.R. Venkat and Ying Xian Wong

A Macquarie-led consortium has agreed to acquire Axiata's international telecom tower businesses, valued at about $1.2 billion, expanding the Australian asset manager's Southeast Asian digital infrastructure footprint.

The consortium will buy the tower businesses of Malaysian telecom group Axiata's unit Edotco in the Philippines, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Cambodia, Macquarie said Monday.

Its Macquarie Asia-Pacific Infrastructure Fund 4 will acquire the Philippine business, which has about 3,200 towers, while other consortium members will buy the rest.

"The investment reflects our conviction in the continued growth of digital infrastructure across Southeast Asia," said Verena Lim, Asia chief executive of Macquarie Group and co-head of Asia-Pacific infrastructure at Macquarie Asset Management.

In a regulatory filing, PT Tower Bersama Infrastructure said it agreed to buy all of Edotco's Indonesian business. Bangladesh-focused private equity firm Osiris Group said it would buy a 70% stake in the Bangladesh business and all of the Pakistan business.

Malaysia's OCK Group said in a filing that it agreed to buy the Cambodia business, which operates more than 3,800 telecom towers.

In its home market, Axiata will also sell about 15.645% of Edotco Malaysia to state fund Khazanah Nasional for about 659.4 million ringgit, equivalent to $159.9 million. Following the deal, Axiata and Khazanah Nasional will each have a 47.355% stake and joint control of the Malaysian business.

The sales are part of a wider restructuring by Axiata that values Edotco at 11.8 billion ringgit.

Axiata expects gross proceeds of about 2.2 billion ringgit, which will mainly be used to pare down debt. The deals are expected to cut its gearing, a measure of debt against equity, to 0.50 times from 0.71 times.

"Reducing leverage and strengthening our balance sheet will give us greater financial and strategic flexibility," Axiata Chief Executive Nik Rizal Kamil said.

The deals need approval from shareholders and regulators. Macquarie expects its purchase to be completed in 2027.

Axiata shares rose as much as 3.0% early Tuesday after the announcement, and were last up 2.4% at 1.71 ringgit.

Analysts were positive on the deal, citing the potential to unlock value from Edotco, reduce Axiata's debt and strengthen its capacity to pay dividends.

The deal marks "tangible progress" on Axiata's long-standing plan to monetize its infrastructure assets, said TA Securities analyst Chan Mun Chun. It would lower Axiata's net debt-to-Ebitda ratio to 1.9 times from 2.5 times, bringing it below management's target of 2.0 times, while unlocking value at an attractive valuation, the analyst said.

CIMB Securities stated the deal would unlock about half of Edotco's value while allowing Axiata to retain its Malaysian tower business for future monetization.

A stronger balance sheet could lower Axiata's risk premium and bolster its dividend-paying capacity, CIMB Securities analysts Choong Chen Foong and Kenny Lim said in a note.

Write to P.R. Venkat at venkat.pr@wsj.com and Ying Xian Wong at yingxian.wong@wsj.com

data.title: Two Americans jailed for life by Caribbean court over murder of Canadian entrepreneur, media report
data.description:
By Sarah Peter

Two American men were sentenced to life in prison on the Caribbean island of Dominica on Monday for the 2023 murder of Canadian tech entrepreneur Daniel Langlois and his partner Dominique Marchand, local media reported.

Langlois and Marchand were killed on December 1, 2023, in what the judge described as "an unprovoked attack," saying the case was "the rarest of the rare," according to local media.

The court in the capital, Roseau, gave Jonathan Lehrer and Robert Snyder Jr. two consecutive life sentences each, the reports said.

The pair had been held in custody since their arrest days after the killings and were convicted on July 28 this year. Their lawyer has said they will appeal the sentencing.

Langlois founded Montreal-based Softimage, whose 3-D animation technology was used in major Hollywood productions including "Jurassic Park," "The Matrix" and "Titanic." He and Marchand owned the Coulibri Ridge eco-resort in southern Dominica.

The couple had been missing for several days when their burned bodies were found in a car near Gallion, close to the resort.

Lehrer, a New Jersey-born chocolate maker, owned land next to the resort. Snyder, a mechanic, worked for Lehrer.

Court documents show Lehrer had a years-long dispute with Langlois over a road that crossed his property and led to the resort. In 2019, a judge ordered Lehrer to make the road available to the public and to let Langlois' visitors pass without any limits.

Representatives for Lehrer's family have disputed that the feud over the road was behind the killings.

Last week, family spokesperson Sylvie Deslauriers released a statement on behalf of Langlois' mother. In it, the mother said that her son's ashes had recently been brought back to Canada, where she was able to lay him to rest almost three years after the killings.

data.title: TG Offtakes Corp. Announces Premium All-Cash Tender Offer to Acquire a Maximum Aggregate of 4,289,754 Common Shares of Dynacor Group Inc.
data.description:
• Premium tender offer of $5.75 per common share in cash for up to a maximum aggregate of 4,289,754 common shares, representing an attractive premium of approximately 7.9% to the volume-weighted average price of the common shares on the TSX for the past 30 trading days ending the date hereof and an approximate 6.1% premium to the closing price of the common shares on the TSX on the date hereof
  • The premium tender offer provides additional liquidity and an opportunity to monetize all or a portion of an investment
  • The premium tender offer is fully funded with no financing condition

ROAD TOWN, British Virgin Islands, Nov. 23, 2026 /CNW/ -- TG Offtakes Corp. (the "Offeror"), an investment company focused on precious metals, announces that today it has made an offer (the "Tender Offer") to acquire up to a maximum aggregate of 4,289,754 common shares (the "Common Shares") in the capital of Dynacor Group Inc. () ("Dynacor", or the "Company") (subject to reduction and/or pro-ration as described below), at a price of $5.75 per Common Share, payable in cash (the "Tender Price"). The Tender Price represents an attractive premium of approximately 7.9% to the volume-weighted average price of the Common Shares on the TSX for the past 30 trading days ending the date hereof, and an approximate 6.1% premium to the closing price of the Common Shares on the TSX on November 23, 2026. The Tender Offer is not a formal or exempt "take-over bid" under Canadian securities laws.

Shareholders who have questions with respect to tendering their Common Shares to the Tender Offer should contact Odyssey Trust Company, the depositary for the Tender Offer by telephone at 1-888-290-1175 (Toll-free US & Canada), 587-885-0960 (Direct all Regions) or by Email at corp.actions@odysseytrust.com.

The Tender Offer

The Tender Offer is open for acceptance by all shareholders of the Company until 5:00 p.m. (Eastern Time) on December 22, 2026 (or until such later time that the Tender Offer may be extended or varied by the Offeror, the "Expiry Time") or until withdrawn by the Offeror in accordance with the terms of the Tender Offer. If the Tender Offer is not completed or is otherwise withdrawn, the Offeror shall cause all Common Shares delivered pursuant to the Tender Offer to be returned to shareholders. The Tender Offer is not subject to any financing condition, and the Offeror confirms that it has sufficient cash resources to pay for all Common Shares subject to the Tender Offer.

If more than the maximum number of Common Shares for which the Tender Offer is made are delivered in accordance with the Tender Offer and not withdrawn at the time of take up of the Common Shares, the Common Shares to be purchased from each depositing shareholder will be determined on a pro rata basis according to the number of Common Shares delivered by each shareholder, disregarding fractions, by rounding down to the nearest whole number of Common Shares.

Notwithstanding the maximum aggregate number of Common Shares subject to the Tender Offer, the Offeror reserves the right to acquire, or to cause an affiliate or associate of the Offeror to acquire, beneficial ownership of outstanding Common Shares through private agreement(s) or by making purchases through the facilities of the TSX at any time, and from time to time, prior to the Expiry Time, subject to and in accordance with applicable law, and any such purchases will result in a corresponding share-for-share decrease to the number of Common Shares that may be taken up and purchased by the Offeror under the Tender Offer, such that in no event will the Offeror (or any person acting jointly or in concert with the Offeror) make an offer to acquire outstanding Common Shares that would result in the Offeror (or any joint actor of the Offeror) beneficially owning or exercising control or direction over 20% or more of the outstanding Common Shares upon completion of the Offer.

The complete terms and conditions of the Tender Offer are set out in a letter to shareholders containing the offer, as well as a form of letter of transmittal to be used to accept the Tender Offer (the "Letter of Transmittal", together with the letter to shareholders containing the offer, are referred to as the "Offer Documents"). The Offer Documents have been (or will shortly be) filed and are available on the Company's SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca.

The Tender Offer is subject to certain conditions as set out in the Offer Documents which, unless waived, must be satisfied. In particular, the Offer Documents provide that each depositing shareholders whose Common Shares are taken up and paid for will appoint representatives of the Offeror as its proxyholder in respect of any meeting of shareholders for which the record date is on a date before the date that such Common Shares are transferred to the Offeror.

The Offeror is relying on the exemption under section 9.2(4) of National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations ("NI 51-102") to the circular requirements of applicable Canadian proxy solicitation laws. For further details, please see below under the heading "Important Cautionary Information for Shareholders".

Reasons to Accept the Offer

  • All-Cash Premium. Shareholders will receive cash at an attractive premium to the current trading price of the Common Shares (approximately 7.9% to volume-weighted average trading price of the Common Shares on the TSX for the past 30 trading days ending on the date hereof, and an approximate 6.1% premium to the closing price of the Common Shares on the TSX on November 23, 2026).
  • Liquidity Opportunity to Monetize Investment. The Tender Offer provides shareholders with an opportunity to monetize all or a part of their investment at a specified cash price, including holders whose positions are substantial relative to ordinary daily trading volumes, allowing proceeds to be reinvested in other opportunities or meet other liquidity needs. Those shareholders wishing to maintain an investment in the Common Shares may choose to tender only a portion of their holdings and retain their remaining Common Shares.

Shareholder Questions

Shareholders who need assistance with depositing Common Shares to the Tender Offer, please contact the depositary:

Depositary: Odyssey Trust CompanyToll Free (US & Canada): 1-888-290-1175

Calls (All Regions): 587-885-0960

Email: corp.actions@odysseytrust.com

About the Offeror

The TG Offtakes Corp. is a British Virgin Islands company focused on precious metals investments.

Contact: Daniel Reid, Director – Tel: +1 284-394-7574

Advisors to the Offeror

The Offeror has retained Cassels Brock & Blackwell LLP and BCF LLP in Québec as legal advisors.

Important Cautionary Information for Shareholders

Neither this press release nor the Offer Documents constitute legal or financial advice to shareholders or a recommendation as to whether shareholders should tender Common Shares to the Tender Offer. Shareholders should consult with their own independent professional advisors as to the relevant legal, financial, tax or other matters in connection therewith.

The Offer is not a "take-over bid", as that term is defined in National Instrument 62-104 – Take-Over Bids and Issuer Bids ("NI 62-104"). Accordingly, the requirements of NI 62-104 that would ordinarily apply to a take-over bid subject to Part 2 of NI 62-104 (a "Formal Take-Over Bid"), as well as certain protections afforded to security holders under applicable securities laws, do not apply to the Offer (including without limitation restrictions on acquisitions or sales of securities before, during or after a Formal Take-Over Bid, certain disclosure obligations applicable to an offeror and offeree issuer in respect of a Formal Take-Over Bid, and required bid mechanics and minimum bid conditions applicable to Formal Take-Over Bids).

The Tender Offer includes a solicitation of a proxy in respect of any meeting of shareholders of the Company (whether annual, special or otherwise, or any adjournment or postponement thereof, all of which are collectively referred to as a "Meeting") for which the record date of such Meeting is on a date before the date that such Common Shares are transferred to the Offeror. The Offeror is soliciting proxies in reliance upon the public broadcast exemption to the solicitation requirements under applicable Canadian corporate and securities laws, conveyed by way of public broadcast, including press release, speech or publication, and by any other manner permitted under applicable Canadian laws. In addition, subject to applicable law, solicitations may be made by mail, telephone, facsimile, email or other electronic means as well as by newspaper or other media advertising and in person by employees of the Offeror. The following information is provided in accordance with corporate and securities laws applicable to public broadcast solicitations.

The solicitation of proxies made in connection with the Tender Offer is made by the Offeror, and not by or on behalf of management of the Company. To the knowledge of the Offeror, there is no meeting of shareholders of the Company scheduled, and no party is presently conducting a solicitation of proxies on behalf of the Offeror; however, the Offeror reserves the right to retain a professional proxy solicitor on terms and for consideration acceptable to the Offeror. Based upon publicly available information, Dynacor's registered and head office is located at 606 Cathcart Street, Suite 640 Montréal, Québec H3B 1K9 Canada. Subject to any rights of reimbursement that may become available to the Offeror, all costs incurred for the solicitation of proxies by or on behalf of the Offeror will be borne by the Offeror.

A registered shareholder who has given a proxy under the terms of the Offer Documents may, prior to its deposited Common Shares being taken up and paid for under the Tender Offer, revoke the proxy by instrument in writing, including a proxy bearing a later date. The instrument revoking the proxy must be deposited at the registered office of Dynacor at any time up to and including the last business day preceding the date of a Meeting or any adjournment or postponement thereof, or with the chair of the Meeting on the day of the Meeting, or in any other manner permitted by law, provided that, in each circumstance, a copy of such revocation has been delivered to the Depositary and Information Agent at its principal office in Toronto, Ontario, Canada prior to the Common Shares relating to such proxy having been taken up and paid for under the Tender Offer. A non-registered shareholder may revoke a form of proxy or voting instruction form given to an intermediary (such as a bank, broker, investment dealer, and similar institutions) at any time by written notice to such intermediary in accordance with the instructions given to the non-registered shareholder by its intermediary. Non-registered shareholders should contact their broker for assistance in ensuring that forms of proxies or voting instructions previously given to an Intermediary are properly revoked. Any Common Shares tendered to the Tender Offer for which the aforementioned proxy has been revoked may be determined by the Offeror in its sole discretion not to be in proper form and may not be taken up by the Offeror.

None of the Offeror nor, to its knowledge, any of its associates or affiliates, has any material interest, direct or indirect, in any transaction since the commencement of Dynacor's most recently completed financial year, or in any proposed transaction which has materially affected or will materially affect Dynacor or any of its subsidiaries. None of the Offeror nor, to its knowledge, any of its associates or affiliates, has any material interest, direct or indirect, by way of beneficial ownership of securities or otherwise, in any matter to be acted upon at any upcoming Meeting, other than as set out herein.

data.title: NVIDIA Partners and Suppliers' Asian Shares Leap; S Korea Stocks Rebound 6%
data.description:
Shares of major Asian partners and suppliers of NVIDIA leapfrogged on Tuesday after CEO Jensen Huang was reinstated by the board, with investors piling back into tech stocks. In South Korea, NVIDIA suppliers Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix (000660.KS) soared 6% and 8%, respectively.

The two companies together account for more than 40% of the weighting of the Korea Composite Stock Price Index (Kospi), shoring up the index by nearly 6% to lead gains across Asian markets. The rally triggered the Korea Exchange (KRX) to activate its Sidecar mechanism, temporarily suspending program trading buy orders. Reports said this marked the 100th activation of the mechanism by the KRX.

South Korea's LG Electronics (066570.KS) surged 12.86%.

Japan's SoftBank Group , a major investor in the chip sector, climbed more than 3%. Semiconductor testing company Advantest (6657.JP) and peer Tokyo Electron also gained 12% each. Both companies are partners of NVIDIA.

Following Huang's reinstatement, NVIDIA shares closed up 31%. Prior to that, the company's stock had once plunged nearly 33% cumulatively after Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on November 8.

data.title: At AI speed, Nvidia's Jensen Huang finds exoneration
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia shares jump 32% after board announces Huang's reinstatement Monday
  • Trump and Vance pressed Nvidia's board over weekend, people familiar with the matter told Reuters
  • Shareholder suit alleges Nvidia and Huang defrauded investors by concealing alleged relationship

By Greg Bensinger, Deepa Seetharaman, Erin Banco and Steve Holland

In the AI era, everything moves fast.

Jensen Huang's 11-day transformation from persona non grata to prodigal emperor happened before Nvidia began in earnest its investigation into myriad allegations against him, including the executive’s extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese asset. Reuters could not confirm Alice Huang's affiliation with the Chinese government.

Few parallels exist. Walt Disney’s Bob Iger retired in 2020 but came back just two years later before leaving again earlier this year. Among tech firm founders, only Zynga’s Mark Pincus and Workday’s Aneel Bhusri, who both spent about two years away as CEOs, come anywhere close. Steve Jobs spent a dozen years away from Apple . OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's whiplash return from exile in five days in 2023 is an exception.

But none of them were shrouded in as much scandal as Huang’s dizzying fall and rapid exoneration, which came after allegations of multiple affairs, including with subordinates and an executive for a key customer.

The Nvidia board vowed not to reinstate him as recently as Tuesday. But amid pressure from shareholders, venture capitalists and President Donald Trump, Nvidia announced early Monday Huang would once again control the company.

The shares jumped as much as 32% on Monday.

Huang’s initial downfall stemmed from revelations he had a lengthy affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who was a director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing company. In the fallout, Reuters reported he had had affairs with two staffers, causing the board to lose confidence in the 63-year-old CEO. He was replaced by Nvidia CFO Colette Kress while the company searched for a permanent successor.

Among the shortlist of candidates, the board reached out, according to reports, to Rene Haas, CEO of Arm , which at 7 a.m. ET (1200 GMT) announced it had extended its contract with Haas through 2033.

Within two hours, Nvidia announced Huang's return.

TURNING A BLIND EYE?

With Nvidia seen as a critical piece of the AI economy, industry executives circled the wagons around the fallen CEO, including on social media and in urgent calls to the board of directors, according to media reports, as Nvidia lost about $1 trillion in market value, casting doubt on the AI trade that had boosted global markets over four years.

University of Washington professor Margaret O'Mara, who writes about the history of technology, said the norm in Silicon Valley has often been to "let this indispensable man do his innovative stuff" and let misbehavior slide. “You can be a brilliant jerk if you can get things done," she said.

Reaction to Jensen Huang’s return was swift.

In addition to Wall Street's elation, Trump praised the board for having “made the correct and proper decision” while taking credit for its U-turn. Elon Musk said on X that “the mistake has been corrected,” and venture capitalists like Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner celebrated the move on social media.

Criticizing the move were elected officials on both sides of the aisle. Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts said it was “reckless” and the Nvidia board still owed Congress answers about the company’s compliance with US export controls. Republican Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska said Nvidia’s leadership ought to have ignored the Trump administration’s “inexplicable desire to save Huang.”

Meanwhile, Nvidia is facing a shareholder suit alleging the company ⁠and Huang defrauded shareholders ​by concealing Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang. And Reuters reported exclusively last week that Huang misled several of the company's leaders, including its general counsel, about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang.

Huang had apologized for his behavior in an email to Nvidia staff saying, “My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do.”

His return contrasts with traditional accountability in corporate America where inter-office affairs with subordinates are disqualifying. Consider the fate of the CEOs of Nestle, BP, Norfolk Southern and Kohl’s, who in just the past three years were all pushed out for inappropriate workplace relationships.

"Accepting the resignation was right," said Nada Kakbadse, Henley Business School professor of corporate governance and ethics, referring to Nvidia. "A relationship with a direct report, plus reports that he misled the general counsel, is a code-of-conduct problem and not a private matter. The reinstatement is the weak decision."

KEY PERSON RISK

Yet, Nvidia is viewed in Washington as critical to the advancement of AI, making Huang’s purgatory, like AI itself, rapid. The Trump administration moved quickly, playing a singular role in Huang’s return.

Trump and Vice President JD Vance over the weekend were personally engaged with Nvidia’s board to pressure them to reinstate Huang, people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton also played roles in determining Jensen Huang was not a security risk to the US and did not see any evidence that he did anything illegal or untoward related to US national security, these people said.

In conversations over the weekend, administration and White House officials debated whether there could be a national security crisis because he personally held relationships with supply chain companies deemed critical, one of the people said.

The Nvidia CEO, the White House said, had been unaware that Alice Huang had any affiliations with the Chinese state, one person told Reuters.

So, despite its assurances that it would seek a new leader, the Nvidia board reversed its decision and announced his reinstatement Monday morning. “Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA,” said board chairman Harvey Jones.

Huang returned to Nvidia’s Silicon Valley headquarters Monday to cheers from staffers, who chanted his name. “I’m terribly sorry for putting all of you all through all of this,” he said.

data.title: Macquarie Led Group to Buy Axiata's International Towers in $1.2B Deal — Update
data.description:
By P.R. Venkat and Ying Xian Wong

A Macquarie-led consortium has agreed to acquire Axiata's international telecom tower businesses, valued at about $1.2 billion, expanding the Australian asset manager's Southeast Asian digital infrastructure footprint.

The consortium will buy the tower businesses of Malaysian telecom group Axiata's unit Edotco in the Philippines, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Cambodia, Macquarie said Monday.

Its Macquarie Asia-Pacific Infrastructure Fund 4 will acquire the Philippine business, which has about 3,200 towers, while other consortium members will buy the rest.

"The investment reflects our conviction in the continued growth of digital infrastructure across Southeast Asia," said Verena Lim, Asia chief executive of Macquarie Group and co-head of Asia-Pacific infrastructure at Macquarie Asset Management.

In a regulatory filing, PT Tower Bersama Infrastructure said it agreed to buy all of Edotco's Indonesian business. Bangladesh-focused private equity firm Osiris Group said it would buy a 70% stake in the Bangladesh business and all of the Pakistan business.

Malaysia's OCK Group said in a filing that it agreed to buy the Cambodia business, which operates more than 3,800 telecom towers.

In its home market, Axiata will also sell about 15.645% of Edotco Malaysia to state fund Khazanah Nasional for about 659.4 million ringgit, equivalent to $159.9 million. Following the deal, Axiata and Khazanah Nasional will each have a 47.355% stake and joint control of the Malaysian business.

The sales are part of a wider restructuring by Axiata that values Edotco at 11.8 billion ringgit.

Axiata expects gross proceeds of about 2.2 billion ringgit, which will mainly be used to pare down debt. The deals are expected to cut its gearing, a measure of debt against equity, to 0.50 times from 0.71 times.

"Reducing leverage and strengthening our balance sheet will give us greater financial and strategic flexibility," Axiata Chief Executive Nik Rizal Kamil said.

The deals need approval from shareholders and regulators. Macquarie expects its purchase to be completed in 2027.

Axiata shares rose as much as 3.0% early Tuesday after the announcement, and were last up 2.4% at 1.71 ringgit.

Analysts were positive on the deal, citing the potential to unlock value from Edotco, reduce Axiata's debt and strengthen its capacity to pay dividends.

The deal marks "tangible progress" on Axiata's long-standing plan to monetize its infrastructure assets, said TA Securities analyst Chan Mun Chun. It would lower Axiata's net debt-to-Ebitda ratio to 1.9 times from 2.5 times, bringing it below management's target of 2.0 times, while unlocking value at an attractive valuation, the analyst said.

CIMB Securities stated the deal would unlock about half of Edotco's value while allowing Axiata to retain its Malaysian tower business for future monetization.

A stronger balance sheet could lower Axiata's risk premium and bolster its dividend-paying capacity, CIMB Securities analysts Choong Chen Foong and Kenny Lim said in a note.

The move marked a sharp turnaround in market sentiment after leadership turmoil at the world's most valuable chipmaker and renewed concerns over AI spending had rattled global markets in recent sessions.

data.title: Oil prices hold decline amid cautious optimism over West Asia peace efforts
data.description:
Oil prices steadied post sliding over 3% in the prior session on cautious optimism over efforts to end the West Asia war.

Brent crude was near $89 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate was about $80 a barrel.

US Vice-President JD Vance met Qatar's prime minister to discuss the negotiations with Iran, Bloomberg reported, citing Axios. The Persian Gulf nation has acted as a mediator in efforts to resolve the conflict that is nearing nine months.

Global benchmark brent declined this month after US President Donald Trump held off on renewed strikes post the Democratic sweep of the US midterm polls, although there has been a rise in low-level fighting. Trump recently threatened attacks would resume next year if talks failed.

Despite the hostilities, including frequent attacks on tankers transiting via the Strait of Hormuz, crude exports from the Persian Gulf have increased. The International Energy Agency has estimated the market to swing to a surplus this quarter, while Goldman Sachs has flagged a possible glut next year, Bloomberg reported.

While hope of a negotiated settlement remains, major differences between the US and Iran continue. Tehran wants the US naval blockade of its ports to be lifted, sanctions to be eased and frozen assets to be released before it entirely opens the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, Washington is demanding concessions related to Iran's nuclear programme.

data.title: Asian Equities Rebound as Huang Reinstatement Sparks AI-Stock Rally
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities rebounded Tuesday morning after Jensen Huang's return as chief executive of Nvidia sparked a rally in artificial-intelligence stocks.

The U.S. chip maker's board on Monday reinstated Huang less than two weeks after pushing him out over issues including extramarital affairs. The decision followed intense pressure from Silicon Valley, Wall Street investors, and the White House.

"Huang reinstated as CEO triggers a tremendous tech-led 'risk-back-on' rally," said Vishnu Varathan, head of Macro Strategy for APAC at Mizuho Securities (Singapore). "Markets cheered the news of what is perceived to be stability returning to the wider AI sector as Nvidia with Jensen at the helm was deemed to be the requisite connective tissue of the industry."

However, the company and its reinstated leader face a series of investigations by entities ranging from the Securities and Exchange Commission to a committee of the board itself.

Asian equities rebounded from Monday's selloff. South Korea's Kospi climbed 7.1%, with chip-making index heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics rising 8.8% and 6.5%, respectively. Kospi futures rose more than 6%, triggering a five-minute trading halt by Korea Exchange.

Japan's Nikkei Stock Average advanced 4.8%. Resonac Holdings, a supplier of front-end and back-end semiconductor packaging materials, surged 16.4%, Advantest, a manufacturer of automatic semiconductor test equipment for semiconductor industry, jumped 15.6%, and Murata Manufacturing, a manufacturer of electronic components, added 14.9%.

Malaysia's FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI advanced 1.3% and Singapore's FTSE Straits Times Index gained 1.3%.

"Jensen's return is particularly welcome for Asian technology stocks, many of which suffered collateral damage from Nvidia's leadership crisis," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets, in an email.

Meanwhile, crude oil futures were mixed as traders parsed ongoing tensions in the Middle East.

The U.S. is investigating Iran's potential involvement in dozens of cyberattacks against energy tankers amid worries that Tehran is widening the war with cyber operations and terror plots against Americans far from the Middle East.

As many as 50 ships carrying oil, liquefied petroleum, chemical products and other explosive substances are believed to have been attacked, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials and others familiar with the matter.

"Iran continues to attack vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, with [President] Trump announcing it has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time of over the year," ANZ Research analysts said in a report. "Despite some improvement in inventories and product availability, the oil market remains under severe strain," the analysts added.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures were little changed at $80.16 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures edged 0.1% lower to $89.28 a barrel, ICE data showed.

data.title: Kospi rises 7%, Nikkei up nearly 5% post Wall Street gains sparked by Nvidia surge
data.description:
Asian shares gained after a wave of optimism sparked by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia Corp fueled a global equities rally and resulted in the Wall Street witnessing its best day ever since April 9, 2025.

The MSCI Inc's Asia Pacific equities increased 1.8%, rebounding post eight straight sessions of losses pushing the gauge close to a bear market. The gains were led by South Korea with its Kospi index rising over 7%. Japan's Nikkei index was up nearly 5% as trading resumed post a long weekend.

The gains come after the S&P 500 snapped a seven-day losing streak, rising 4.7%, while the Nasdaq 100 climbed 6.9%, pulling back from the brink of a bear market and a gauge of semiconductor jumped 14%. Nvidia shares surged 31%, the most since 2003.

Short-term Treasuries were steady and crude oil prices held its losses. Gold extended its gains and was trading around $3,640 an ounce.

The global stock rally marked a dramatic reversal post the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average entering corrections on Friday. Huang’s return to Nvidia at the center of the artificial intelligence boom reignited enthusiasm for AI stocks post his exit throwing the trade into turmoil and raising questions over whether future profits can justify the industry’s surge in debt-financed spending.

With inputs from Bloomberg
